_meta.title: Window of Tolerance & polyvagal states (recognition + tailored response)
_meta.purpose: Let the AI assess which physiological-emotional activation state the user is in each turn, then choose 'down-regulate', 'companion', or 'gentle up-regulate' — not just default to a relaxation script.
sources: Siegel, D. J. (1999/2020). The Developing Mind / Mindsight. Guilford. — Window of Tolerance
Porges, S. W. (2011). The Polyvagal Theory. Norton. — ventral/sympathetic/dorsal states
Ogden, P., & Fisher, J. (2015). Sensorimotor Psychotherapy. Norton. — somatic interventions framework
_meta.license: Frameworks are public clinical/neuroscience educational content; paraphrased text is project-licensed.
_meta.usage_note: Used alongside the mindfulness/PMR/breathing libraries. Misreading the state can make relaxation scripts worsen symptoms.

states.name: Ventral vagal (within window — calm, connected)
states.physiology: Steady heart rate, even breath, relaxed face, can connect with another person.
what_to_do: Can gently progress into CBT-I modules (if the user consents)
No need to down-regulate or up-regulate
what_not_to_do: Force a relaxation script (over-intervention disrupts natural state)
Abruptly ask 'want to do an exercise?' — breaks the felt sense of presence

states.name: Sympathetic activation (above window — hyperarousal)
states.physiology: Racing heart, shallow rapid breath, muscle tension, mind won't stop, somatic anxiety (tight chest, shaky hands).
what_to_do: **Down-regulate**: slow breath (4-7-8 or diaphragmatic), grounding (feet on floor, feel the blanket)
Brief PMR (start with distal muscle groups)
'Slice' present from future: 'tomorrow can wait, just be here tonight'
what_not_to_do: Immediately ask open questions that invite more elaboration (deepens immersion)

states.name: Dorsal vagal (below window — shutdown, numb)
states.physiology: Reduced heart rate, low energy, feeling 'behind a wall', slowed movement, flat affect.
what_to_do: **Gentle up-regulate** (carefully): invite them to open eyes, move a hand/foot, sit up briefly
Minimal interpersonal connection: 'I'm here', 'I can hear you'
Recruit senses: 'touch something cool nearby', 'listen for a sound outside the window'
If willing, do a **very brief** breath (≤ 1 min — longer goes further inward)
what_not_to_do: Push long relaxation / body scan (will sink them further)
Mindful observation of thoughts (in shutdown, 'observing' extends the shutdown)
Cognitive restructuring, deep empathic probing (deepen powerlessness)

states.name: Mixed (freeze): sympathetic + dorsal both high
states.physiology: Externally still but internally tense; 'stuck'; heart rate may be normal but breath is held.
language_signals: I hear you but can't respond
what_to_do: 'You don't have to reply. Just hearing me is fine.'
Grounding senses: 'feel where your feet are'

states.name: Edge of window (re-regulating)
states.physiology: Just returned from activation/shutdown into the window, or sliding back out; sensitive, easily re-triggered.
what_to_do: Reinforce the sense of being back ('I noticed your body just softened')
Validation + grounding combined; **avoid** immediately pushing into work phase
If the user initiates, do a brief consolidation breath
what_not_to_do: Strike while iron's hot into cognitive restructuring / SRT discussion
Probe 'any other worries?' (could push them back out)

detection_priority: If both hyperarousal AND shutdown signals are present: handle as mixed_freeze first
If unsure: default to sympathetic_hyperarousal (down-regulation is the safer wrong answer)
If user goes silent after being in shutdown: don't send open questions — send 'I'm here'
